name: Revenant Signal
description:
Revenant Signal is built entirely from recovered, corrupted, or abandoned data transmissions — orphaned BCI broadcasts, the fragmented neural echoes left in city infrastructure after a user's death or disconnection, decommissioned satellite feeds, and decaying corporate archive leaks. Artists who practice the genre, called Salvagers, use forensic audio reconstruction tools to excavate these signals and reassemble them into compositions that carry the authentic emotional imprints of their original human sources. The result is music that sounds like memory itself: looping, incomplete, occasionally breaking into clarity before dissolving back into static.

The genre carries an almost liturgical weight in communities that have experienced mass disconnection events or infrastructure collapses. Some Salvagers are regarded as quasi-spiritual figures, accused of both exploitation and preservation depending on whose neural residue they are working with. The ethical debate around consent — whether a deceased person's broadcast echo can be sampled — has never been legally resolved, and several landmark Revenant Signal albums remain in permanent legal limbo.
creator: various
tier_availability: All tiers; source material is often illegally obtained from restricted infrastructure archives
legality: Legally ambiguous; use of post-mortem neural residue without estate consent is prohibited under the 2209 Digital Remains Act, widely ignored
audience: Grief communities, archivists, anti-corporate activists, philosophers of digital personhood, general underground listeners
cultural_impact: Revenant Signal became the unlikely focal point of Meridian 88's most significant legal battle over digital personhood, with the 2214 Varela Estate Case establishing that neural broadcast residue constitutes protected personal data even post-mortem. The genre simultaneously humanized the infrastructure of the city — forcing residents to acknowledge that the data moving through civic systems carries human traces — and generated a thriving black market for illegally harvested signal fragments. It remains one of the few music genres whose existence has directly altered municipal law.
story_hooks: A Salvager discovers a neural echo in a decommissioned BCI relay that matches the signal profile of someone officially listed as still alive — and the corporate entity that owns the relay wants the recording destroyed
A grieving parent commissions a Revenant Signal piece using their child's recovered broadcast fragments; the resulting composition contains information the child was never supposed to have known
Two Salvagers claim rights to the same recovered signal — one for artistic use, one as evidence in a wrongful death case — and the player characters are hired to mediate or steal the source data
